environment.tool: manual audit of the tag source + live compiled binary; raw hex request bytes, exact-token peer plus an independent naive concatenating upstream

findings.description: `/api/../exec?cmd=id` decodes to path `/api/../exec`; the rewrite emits `"/"+path.substr(4)` = `/../exec`, so the peer receives `GET //../exec?cmd=id`. The proxy has removed the `/api` prefix the client typed and handed the `..` to the upstream untouched. Proven twice: the exact-token peer echoes `RAW=b'GET //../exec?cmd=id HTTP/1.1'` with `TOKS=3 EXEC=1`, and an independent naive concatenating upstream (no normalisation, opens ROOT+token[1]) returns `EXEC-ONE-LEVEL-UP` from `/tmp/.../up//../exec` instead of `EXEC-AT-UPDOCROOT` from the control's `/tmp/.../up//exec` — a different file. 3/3 from cold on both upstreams; `%2e%2e` behaves identically.
findings.title: The `..` guard runs only in the static branch, so a proxied `..` reaches the upstream request line and escapes a level

limitations: The proxy never executes; all RCE is on the upstream host
Needs a proxied prefix location and an upstream that resolves `..`
